PlantInfo identifies a plant, a tree or a mushroom from your photos, then gathers what you need to know into a single record: description, condition, habitat, distribution area, edibility and toxicity. You can then ask your own questions about the identified species.
These calls leave from your phone, so each service sees your IP address, like any visit to a website. What they keep of it is governed by their own terms of use.
PlantInfo hosts no identification service of its own: it queries the ones that already exist, using your own accounts. That is what lets the app charge you nothing and keep nothing on its side.
Nothing is final: you can add, replace or clear a key at any time in the Settings, and start this assistant again from the same screen.
You can skip this step and come back to it later.
Everything is in place. Photograph a plant and start an identification.
You can identify plants with Pl@ntNet. Without an AI key, the record is limited to the species name: no description, no condition, no mushrooms and no questions.
You can identify with the AI alone, mushrooms included. Without Pl@ntNet, the botanical check that makes the species name reliable is missing.
No key is saved: identification will not be able to start. Start this assistant again from the Settings when you are ready.

string-array.name: setup_where_data_lives

resources.string: An API key is a password you create at an online service (Pl@ntNet, Google, Anthropic, OpenAI) and paste here. It allows PlantInfo to query that service on your behalf, from your phone. There is no PlantInfo account: each key stays encrypted on this device and is only sent to the service it belongs to.

To get started, two keys are enough: Pl@ntNet (identification, free) and Gemini (description, condition, mushrooms). Gemini\'s free tier works, but it is slow and limited to a few dozen requests a day; with billing enabled, expect %1$s. Claude and GPT are optional alternatives, also paid for.

Pl@ntNet is a specialised service: it compares the photo with a database of botanical observations and suggests species, saying nothing else about them. The AI (Gemini) takes that suggestion, checks it against the photo, writes the description, assesses the condition, handles mushrooms — which Pl@ntNet does not cover — and answers your questions. With Pl@ntNet alone you get a name; with the AI alone you lose the botanical check.
Identifies the species from the photo. It is the foundation of the app.
Free: signing up gives you a daily identification quota, enough for personal use.
The Pl@ntNet key is already created for you: there is nothing to generate, only the value shown in your account to copy.
Describes the plant, assesses its condition, identifies mushrooms and answers your questions.

The free tier of Google AI Studio is enough to try things out, but it is slow at busy times and caps out at a few dozen requests a day; beyond that, the key stops answering until the next day. Enabling billing on the Google project removes the wait, and you pay %1$s.
The key is only shown in full when it is created: copy it straight away. If you have lost it, simply create a new one.
An alternative to Gemini for the description, the condition and questions. Often the sharpest on tricky species.
Pay as you go, billed by token (a few cents per identification). The account must be topped up before first use.
A Claude Pro or Max subscription includes no API credit: without credit on the developer account, the key is accepted but every call fails.
A second alternative for the description, the condition and questions.

string-array.name: guide_plantnet_steps
string-array.item: Open my.plantnet.org and create an account (email address + password).
Confirm the verification email you receive.
Sign in again, then open the “Settings” of your account.
Find the “API key” line and copy the value shown.
Come back here and paste it with the “paste” button of the field below.

string-array.name: guide_gemini_steps
string-array.item: Open aistudio.google.com/apikey and sign in with a Google account.
Accept the Google AI Studio terms of use if they appear.
Click “Create API key”.
Choose a Google Cloud project when asked — the one offered by default will do.
Copy the key shown (it starts with “AIza”) and paste it below.

string-array.name: guide_claude_steps
string-array.item: Open console.anthropic.com and create an account.
Under “Billing” / “Plans”, add credit (a minimal amount is enough for hundreds of identifications).
Open “Settings” then “API keys”.
Click “Create key” and give it a name (“PlantInfo”, for instance).
Copy the key shown (it starts with “sk-ant-”) and paste it below.

string-array.name: guide_openai_steps
string-array.item: Open platform.openai.com and create an account.
Under “Billing”, add credit to the account.
Open “API keys” from the account menu.
Click “Create new secret key” and confirm.
Copy the key shown (it starts with “sk-”) and paste it below.
